Detailed entries for `QPKG-008..QPKG-011`. Each follows the four-part
**What / Why / How / When NOT to apply** shape.

---

## QPKG-008 — Ship statically linked (musl) binaries

**What.** Native code in a QPKG is statically linked, typically against musl
(`x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl`). Do not link
against the NAS's glibc.

**Why.** QTS glibc is old and not upgraded with firmware: QTS 5.1.8 and 5.2.9
report glibc 2.21, and some models report 2.17
([QNAP community, 2026-10-31](https://community.qnap.com/t/upgrade-outdated-glibc-currently-2-21-in-upcoming-qts-5-2-x-releases/7399)).
Roon dropped QNAP support in 2026 for this reason. A binary built against a
current glibc fails to start with `GLIBC_2.xx not found`, which App Center
reports only as a failed start.

**How.**

```sh
cargo zigbuild --release --target aarch64-unknown-linux-musl
file target/aarch64-unknown-linux-musl/release/myapp   # expect "statically linked"
```

For a release you repackage, prefer the upstream `*-musl` artifact.

**When NOT to apply.** When the app needs a library that cannot be linked
statically, ship that library and its glibc in the package with a launcher
that sets the loader path. That is far more work, so treat it as a last
resort.

## QPKG-009 — Treat kernel page size as a build input on ARM

**What.** Before building for an ARM QNAP, find its kernel page size with
`getconf PAGESIZE` on the target. Do not ship an allocator built for 4 KiB
pages to a kernel with larger ones. Prefer an allocator that reads the page
size at runtime (musl's, mimalloc). If you must use jemalloc, build it with
`JEMALLOC_SYS_WITH_LG_PAGE=16` (64 KiB), which is valid on every smaller page
size.

**Why.** Annapurna AL-314 QNAPs report a 32 KiB page size. Alpine 3.18+ musl
builds segfaulted there
([home-assistant/core#86589](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/86589)).
jemalloc built for 4 KiB pages aborts with
`<jemalloc>: Unsupported system page size` on AL-324 and TS-531P models
([qdrant/qdrant#2474](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/issues/2474), 2023).
tikv-jemalloc-sys documents that the configured page size "must be at least
as large as the system page size"
([tikv/jemallocator](https://github.com/tikv/jemallocator/blob/main/jemalloc-sys/README.md)).

**How.**

```sh
ssh admin@nas getconf PAGESIZE      # e.g. 32768 on AL-314
JEMALLOC_SYS_WITH_LG_PAGE=16 cargo zigbuild --release --target aarch64-unknown-linux-musl
```

**When NOT to apply.** x86_64 QNAPs use 4 KiB pages; the rule is about ARM
models.

## QPKG-010 — Check ARM ELF `LOAD` segment alignment

**What.** Before shipping an ARM binary, check its program headers with
`readelf -lW` and confirm every `LOAD` segment's `Align` is at least the
largest page size you target (`0x10000` covers 64 KiB).

**Why.** A binary linked with 4 KiB segment alignment cannot be mapped on a
kernel with larger pages and fails at exec on those models only, so testing
on a 4 KiB-page board passes. It is a quick, static check that needs no
access to the target.

**How.**

```sh
readelf -lW arm_64/bin/myapp | awk '/LOAD/ {print $NF}'   # expect 0x10000
# when building yourself:
RUSTFLAGS="-C link-arg=-Wl,-z,max-page-size=65536" cargo zigbuild --release --target aarch64-unknown-linux-musl
```

**When NOT to apply.** x86_64 binaries (`Align 0x1000` is correct there).

## QPKG-011 — Verify repackaged upstream releases against published checksums

**What.** When a QPKG wraps an upstream release binary instead of building
it, the build downloads the exact version and verifies it against the
upstream checksum file before packaging. Pin the version in the build.

**Why.** A QPKG runs as root on the NAS (QPKG-012). A binary swapped on a
mirror or changed by a re-tagged release ends up in every user's NAS under
your package name. Pinning also keeps `QPKG_VER` and the shipped binary in
step.

**How.**

```sh
v=1.0.4
curl -fLO "https://github.com/example/app/releases/download/v$v/app-linux-aarch64-musl-v$v.zip"
curl -fLO "https://github.com/example/app/releases/download/v$v/SHA256SUMS"
sha256sum -c --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS
```

**When NOT to apply.** When you build the binary yourself from a pinned
source revision, the checksum step moves to the source download.
